title: CHAPTER THREE. On the knowledge of God; way, mode, and reason of knowing Him
pass_a_gloss: Pass A clause gloss (reordered): CHAPTER THREE. Concerning ye knowledge belonging toward God; where ye way, mode plus reason belonging toward knowing GOD are shown. We have seen that GOD is: now we will show ye way, mode plus reason by which ye nature belonging toward God by a Christian rightly can be known. For in vain we seek ye unknown unless by what way plus power it is to be investigated we first know. His nature a priori cannot be known, because first of all it is. By God alone adequately known. By us to some extent but infinitely lower. Tertullian: nothing of God can be comprehended except that He is incomprehensible. Augustine: God is that which no opinion attains.
pass_b_english: CHAPTER THREE. On the knowledge of God; where the way, mode, and reason of knowing GOD are shown.

We have seen that GOD is: now we will show the way, mode, and reason by which God's nature can rightly be known by a Christian. For in vain we seek what is unknown unless we first know by what way and power it is to be investigated.

His nature cannot be known a priori, because it is first of all (Isaiah 44:6; Revelation 1:8). It is adequately known by God alone. By us it is known to some extent, but infinitely lower (1 Corinthians 13:12). Tertullian: nothing at all can be comprehended of God except that He is incomprehensible. Augustine: God is that which no opinion attains.
source_text: CAPUT TERTIUM, De cognitione Dei; ubi ostenditur via, modus & ratio cognoscendi DEUM. Vidimus DEUM esse: nunc ostendemus viam, modum & rationem qua natura Dei a Christiano recte cognosci potest. Frustra enim quaerimus incognitum, nisi qua via & virtute investigandus sit praenoscimus. Natura illius cognosci nequit a priori: quia omnium prima est, Esa. 44.6; Apoc. 1.8. A Deo solo adaequate cognoscitur. A nobis cognoscitur quadamtenus, sed infinite inferius, 1 Cor. 13.12. Tertullianus: Nihil quicquam de Deo comprehendi potest, nisi quod sit incomprehensibilis. Augustinus: Deus hoc est, quod nulla attingit opinio.
